key_insight: VisDom improves sparse novel view synthesis by adding a "visible domain" constraint, helping models focus on geometry that is actually supported by the input views. This reduces floating artifacts and overly loose reconstructions that often happen with NeRF and Gaussian Splatting in sparse settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reconstructing accurate 3D geometry from only a few input views, where existing methods tend to overfit, hallucinate unsupported regions, and produce inconsistent shapes.
method: Introduces a visible domain constraint to restrict reconstruction to regions plausibly observable from the input views.
Uses this constraint as a regularizer to improve geometric consistency beyond standard silhouette-based losses.
Targets sparse-view settings where NeRF- and Gaussian Splatting-based methods commonly fail due to ambiguity and weak supervision.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to make sparse-view 3D reconstruction more stable and trustworthy. It is especially useful for applications where capturing many views is expensive or impossible.
